findings.text: blocking: export_snapshot returns without writing whenever the stored documents' identity is unchanged, so the station heartbeat captured at :269 is frozen at the last content change; demonstrated on an unchanged fleet, export at t0+121 s returned None, the file still carried heartbeat t0, and read_station_answer reported stale=True with heartbeat_age_seconds=121, so an off-node reader calls a healthy quiet station stopped, the confusion the plan's heartbeat exists to prevent. Refresh the heartbeat into the file on a bounded cadence, or write when its age passes a fraction of the stale window; station.py:207 also publishes before :214 writes the heartbeat, so the first export carries none.

non-blocking: crew view obligations still derives the fleet here instead of calling obligation_snapshot.read_station_answer first and falling back, so the second consumer the goal names is unwired; the reviewed manifest records this under outside_scope and it needs its own node rather than a repair to this one.

non-blocking: station_runtime_candidate duplicates the candidate order owned by reckon/crew/station_store.py:runtime_root_source, which delegates to dispatch_watch.session_host_runtime_candidate, and STATION_DATABASE_NAME at :315 copies station_store.DATABASE_NAME — two definitions the repository already owns, neither of which this addition extends; the stated reason (the module must not import the crew package) does not hold at call time, since reckon.crew is a namespace package with no __init__ and station_store imports only json and sqlite3 at module level, so a lazy import inside the function would extend the owner. tests/test_obligations_read_the_station.py:210 and :213 pin the copies equal, which makes drift detectable but leaves the duplication in place.

non-blocking: _station_producer names the field started_at but sets it to the instant of every refresh, so a stored document reports the station as having started when the obligations were last recomputed, which misleads a reader diagnosing the station.
